quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the pitch of the start: is the noise sharp and high, or broad and lower?
quests.explanation: Here, "sip" started with a sharp, thin /s/. "Ship" starts with a broader hush.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The lips and tongue position both differ, and together they change the colour of the noise.
quests.mouthPosition: Watch your lips: they push forward for /ʃ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: After the first burst, the tongue either taps the ridge or curls back. Which do you hear?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "crime" curled the tongue back. "Climb" taps the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: After /k/, /ɡ/, /p/, /b/ or /f/, the /r/ pulls the lips and tongue back, while /l/ keeps the tongue tip forward.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the lips slightly rounded through the cluster for /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: She wrote sock on the board.
quests.hint: Rounded and open, or tight and thin?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "sock": rounded lips and a dropped jaw. "Sick" stays tight.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Bright and thin (/ɪ/) versus deep and round (/ɒ/) is the simplest way to hear the difference.
quests.mouthPosition: Go from a tight, slightly smiling mouth (/ɪ/) to an open, rounded mouth (/ɒ/).

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: One vowel is short and half open, the other long and high.
quests.explanation: "said" had a crisp, half-open vowel. "Seed" is longer and smiling.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /iː/ is long, tense and high; /e/ is short and mid. Both differ in duration and in how far the tongue rises.
quests.mouthPosition: For /iː/ spread the lips and lift the tongue high. For /e/ lower the jaw halfway and let the lips relax.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both end in a buzz. Sharp or soft?
quests.explanation: That was "breeze": a sharper /z/ buzz. "Breathe" ends in soft friction with the tongue at the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The buzz is present in both, so listen to the quality of the friction: soft and diffuse for /ð/, sharp for /z/.
quests.mouthPosition: Look in a mirror for the tongue tip with /ð/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same frame, same ending. Is the vowel stretched?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "grin" was quick and loose. "Green" would linger on a tense, smiling vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Two things separate these vowels: duration and tongue tension. /iː/ is held longer and sounds bright and tight; /ɪ/ is clipped and sounds softer, almost muffled by comparison.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the jaw nearly closed for both, but make /iː/ tighter: lips spread, tongue pushed high and forward. /ɪ/ needs no effort at all - let everything go slack.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Flat, central vowel or rounded, back one?
quests.explanation: You heard "rub": neutral lips and a central vowel. "Rob" rounds the lips and moves back.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is a back vowel with slight lip rounding; /ʌ/ is a central vowel with neutral lips. /ɒ/ sounds rounder and deeper, /ʌ/ sounds flatter and more central.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɒ/ round the lips lightly and pull the tongue back. For /ʌ/ keep the lips neutral and let the tongue lie in the centre.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the last sound: is it breathy and crisp, or voiced and a touch longer?
quests.explanation: Here, "search" ended with a breathy /tʃ/. "Surge" buzzes.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /tʃ/ and /dʒ/ share the same tongue movement; /tʃ/ is voiceless and /dʒ/ is voiced. The voiced version has a buzz and a longer preceding vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: Press the tongue against the ridge behind the teeth and release into a hush. Keep the throat silent for /tʃ/; add voice for /dʒ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Burst or airy friction at the start?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "tread" began with a stop. "Thread" begins with soft friction at the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /t/ is abrupt; /θ/ is gradual and airy.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the air flow continuously for /θ/ and burst for /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Front or back nasal at the end?
quests.explanation: This time, "king" ended with a back-of-the-tongue nasal. "Kin" ends at the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue touches at the front for /n/ and at the back for /ŋ/, so the vowel before it colours differently.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip behind the lower teeth for /ŋ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both vowels are short. Would your lips round at all, or stay neutral?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "gone" rounded the lips lightly and sounded deeper. "Gun" is neutral and flat.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so rely on lip shape: rounded for /ɒ/, unrounded for /ʌ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Notice your lips: a small circle for /ɒ/, a neutral shape for /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Look at the final sound and the vowel length.
quests.explanation: It was "pens": a buzz at the end and a slightly longer vowel. "Pence" hisses.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, /z/ lengthens the vowel before it and has a soft buzz; /s/ shortens the vowel and ends with a crisp hiss. In final position the buzz can be weak, so vowel length is the most reliable cue.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold the tongue behind the upper teeth. For /s/ end with a sharp hiss after a short vowel; for /z/ stretch the vowel and finish with a softer buzz.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: At the start, does the air stop completely, or does it keep flowing softly?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "true": a burst from the tongue tip. "Through" begins with soft, continuous air.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The stop /t/ blocks the air completely before releasing it; /θ/ never stops the air.
quests.mouthPosition: The tongue is further forward for /θ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Weigh the vowel length and lip rounding together.
quests.explanation: That was "cord": long with rounded lips. "Cod" is short and open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is short with the mouth open and lips slightly rounded; /ɔː/ is long, with the tongue raised further at the back and the lips more clearly rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɔː/ round the lips into a clear circle and let the tongue rise a little at the back. For /ɒ/ open the jaw and round the lips only slightly.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Natural speech: keep your ear on the stressed vowel. Long or short?
quests.explanation: The word was "list": a short, relaxed vowel followed quickly by the /st/. "Least" holds a tense, high vowel longer.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are front and high, but /ɪ/ sits slightly lower and more relaxed. The sound your ear catches first is the difference in length: /iː/ lasts noticeably longer.
quests.mouthPosition: Try saying /iː/ with a wide, tense smile, then relax the cheeks and shorten the sound; that slack, quick version is /ɪ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Friction or a lip closure at the end?
quests.explanation: You heard "curve": buzzing friction. "Curb" closes the lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The stop /b/ blocks the air completely, /v/ never does.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the lips close for /b/ but the teeth touch the lip for /v/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is the vowel deep and rounded, or wide and bright? Forget the ending.
quests.explanation: Here, "stock" was rounded and deep. "Stack" is wide and bright.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is a front vowel with lips slightly spread; /ɒ/ is a back vowel with the lips rounded a little. The tongue moves from front to back and the lip shape changes with it.
quests.mouthPosition: For /æ/ keep the tongue pushed forward and the lips slightly spread. For /ɒ/ pull the tongue back and round the lips a little.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Long and open, or short and blunt?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "barn": a long, wide-open vowel. "Bun" is short and flat.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʌ/ is short, central and made with the jaw fairly relaxed; /ɑː/ is long, back and made with the mouth open wide. Duration and openness both help you hear them apart.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɑː/ drop the jaw wide open and let the tongue lie low and back, as if the doctor said 'say ahh'. For /ʌ/ open only a little and keep everything relaxed and short.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Bright, wide vowel or half open?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "gas" opened the jaw wide. "Guess" is narrower.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ is a short mid-front vowel with the jaw only half open; /æ/ is more open and a little longer, with the jaw dropped and the tongue lowered at the front.
quests.mouthPosition: For /e/ open the jaw about halfway and keep the lips relaxed. For /æ/ drop the jaw further and spread the mouth slightly, as if beginning to yawn sideways.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is the end of the word buzzy and voiced, or breathy and crisp?
quests.explanation: That was "ridge": a voiced /dʒ/ with a slightly longer vowel. "Rich" is breathier.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Voicing is the only change; listen for the buzz in /dʒ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the throat to feel the vibration.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Short or long vowel before the lip closure?
quests.explanation: This time, "cub" had a short, dull vowel. "Carb" lengthens an open one.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɑː/ is the longer, deeper vowel with a wide-open mouth; /ʌ/ is a quick, relaxed sound from the middle of the mouth.
quests.mouthPosition: Open wide and hold it for /ɑː/; for /ʌ/ the jaw is barely open and the sound stops almost as soon as it starts.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does a stop come before the hush?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "march" had a /t/ before the hush. "Marsh" is smooth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are voiceless; the stop part is the clue.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the lips slightly rounded for both.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel glides in both. Listen for how long it lasts and how it ends.
quests.explanation: Here, "dose" ended with a crisp hiss after a slightly shorter glide. "Doze" buzzes.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A longer vowel signals /z/; a shorter vowel and a strong hiss signal /s/.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel your throat vibrate through the end of /z/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Middle consonant: curl or tap?
quests.explanation: The word was "berry": a curled tongue. "Belly" taps the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /l/ sounds clear and light; /r/ sounds darker and slightly rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the tongue tip: contact for /l/, hover for /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the lip touch the teeth?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "wiper" used rounded lips. "Viper" buzzes lip-on-teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The lower lip touches the teeth only for /v/.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue relaxed for both.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: One opening sound is driven by the lips, the other by the tongue.
quests.explanation: It was "wide": rounded lips opening. "Ride" starts with a curled tongue.
quests.vowelTensionRule: For /w/ the lips do the work; for /r/ the tongue does.
quests.mouthPosition: Watch your lips: they move a lot for /w/ and much less for /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the tongue block the air at the start?
quests.explanation: "day" started with a stop. "They" flows with voiced friction at the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /d/ blocks the air completely, /ð/ never does.
quests.mouthPosition: Look in a mirror: the tongue tip peeks out for /ð/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Short, relaxed vowel or long, tense one?
quests.explanation: You heard "still": short and quick. "Steal" stretches the vowel before the /l/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /iː/ is long and tense with the tongue high and forward; /ɪ/ is short, loose and a little lower and more central. Length and tension travel together, so a stretched vowel usually means /iː/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /iː/ spread the lips as if smiling and lift the tongue high behind the lower teeth. For /ɪ/ let the lips relax and drop the tongue a touch.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is the jaw wide or half open before the /nd/?
quests.explanation: That was "band": a wide vowel. "Bend" stays half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The difference is jaw opening. /e/ keeps the mouth half open; /æ/ opens it wide so the vowel sounds fuller and broader.
quests.mouthPosition: Start from /e/, then lower the jaw another centimetre without moving the tongue tip from behind the lower teeth - that wide sound is /æ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Smooth hush or stop-plus-hush at the end?
quests.explanation: The word was "dish": a smooth hush. "Ditch" adds a stop first.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʃ/ is a continuous fricative; /tʃ/ begins with a stop and then releases into friction, so it sounds abrupt at the start. Listen for a sudden beginning versus a smooth flow.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʃ/ let the air flow steadily over the tongue. For /tʃ/ block the air with the tongue against the ridge, then release into a hush.
